In Mission District, walls often want width - long, low compositions that stretch the room. In Downtown San Fernando, the same walnut slat wall tends to run taller and simpler. Starting from your room photo is what lets us tune that rhythm to your street instead of shipping a showroom layout.

A walnut slat wall also solves practical problems: cables disappear, equipment gets ventilation and access, and the TV lands at the right height for your sofa - not wherever the studs happened to be.

How we build a walnut slat wall

Walnut slats change how a room feels more than almost any other single upgrade: warmer, quieter and more finished. We use acoustic slat panels with real walnut veneer on a black felt backing, cut and fitted on site so seams land exactly where the design puts them. Corners, outlets and baseboards are worked around by hand - no gaps, no trim shortcuts. Behind a TV, slats pair with a floating cabinet and backlighting; in an entry or bedroom they carry the room on their own.

Questions from San Fernando homeowners

How much does a walnut slat wall cost in San Fernando?

A walnut slat accent wall in San Fernando starts at $2,500 for a standard TV-wall section. Full-width and floor-to-ceiling layouts are priced by the written estimate after your design preview - materials and labor are itemized, nothing is bundled into a mystery number.

Do slat walls help with echo?

Yes. The felt backing absorbs mid and high frequencies, which is why slat walls are popular in open-plan living rooms and media rooms with hard floors - the room sounds calmer, not just looks it.

Can slats go around corners and doors?

Yes. Panels are cut on site for corners, outlets and door casings, and we offer matching slat-faced hidden doors when a door sits inside the accent wall.

How are slat walls maintained?

A dry or slightly damp microfiber cloth is enough. The veneer is pre-finished; no oiling or sanding is needed.
